findings.title: Missing recurrence is incorrectly treated as high-confidence evidence of task success
findings.where: src/lib/parse-task-success.ts:458-467 and 534-557; behavior asserted by src/lib/parse-task-success.test.ts:181-201 and 245-276
findings.what: When no later matching topic is present in the supplied HistoryEntry array, corroborateSpan raises confidence to high and successScore to at least 0.9. The input has no completeness marker or observation cutoff, and the emitted corroborated provenance contains only a topic. A partial or stale history therefore produces a strong success claim that is neither evidence-backed nor reproducible as of a stated date.
findings.fix: Do not promote absence alone to high confidence. Require explicit, structured observation provenance containing the history coverage/cutoff and source artifact, emit an `as of <date>` qualification, and keep confidence low/unknown when completeness cannot be established.
findings.acceptance: A fixture containing only the completed span, with no declared history coverage, must not produce high confidence or a score of 0.9; a corroborated result must expose a source artifact and observation cutoff, and adding a later matching turn before that cutoff must deterministically prevent corroboration.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read the promotion function, both recurrence loops, and the two locking tests at the immutable baseline. No completeness or cutoff input exists, and the corroborated object records no proof or date; the claim survives.

findings.title: Task-success recurrence analysis is quadratic over history-sized collections
findings.what: For every corrective turn, applyRecurrence filters every span and sorts the matches; it then calls Array.find across all topic turns for every eligible span. With C corrective turns, S spans, and T topic turns, this performs O(C×S log S + S×T) work during dataset assembly, in addition to repeated date parsing and topic intersection checks.
findings.fix: Index spans and turns by recurrence topic and timestamp, then use ordered lookup/binary search to select the latest eligible prior span and detect a bounded-window returning turn without rescanning global arrays; avoid sorting candidate lists inside the loop.
findings.acceptance: Add an ingest benchmark/probe using proportionally scaled spans and turns; doubling equal-sized inputs must remain near linear or O(n log n), and the recurrence results must match existing fixtures.
findings.verifyNote: A separate re-read confirmed the nested full-array filter/sort at lines 503-515 and per-span full-array find at lines 534-553. No topic index, cursor, or early range partition exists at this baseline.

findings.title: Task artifact traversal follows symlinks outside the configured root
findings.what: Session and task paths are formed from directory entries, then validated with statSync, which follows symbolic links. A symlinked session directory or `.json` task file can therefore resolve outside `dir`; readFileSync will ingest the external target if it is a regular JSON file.
findings.fix: Reject symbolic links using Dirent/lstat checks and verify each realpath remains beneath the canonical task root before opening it; preferably open with no-follow semantics where supported and validate the opened file.
findings.acceptance: Create a task-root fixture containing both a symlinked session directory and a symlinked `.json` file pointing outside the root; parseTasksDir must return no records from either while continuing to parse ordinary in-root files.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read the complete traversal loop at the immutable baseline and the directly related bounded directory helper. Directory names are bounded but neither layer rejects symlinks or checks canonical containment, while statSync/readFileSync follow them.
